relationships.subject: TRPA1
relationships.evidence_quote: When activated, TRPA1 can elevate intracellular calcium levels that, in turn, trigger vesicle exocytosis via the action of SNARE proteins and subsequent CGRP release.

key_findings: Chronic oxaliplatin caused cold allodynia and reduced nerve conduction velocity without increasing Calca/CGRP in DRG (unchanged in males, decreased in females), while Ramp1 was upregulated about two-fold.
Authors propose a sensitization/release-based TRPA1-calcium-CGRP mechanism rather than CGRP upregulation in oxaliplatin neuropathy.
